recent_posts.title: Scaling AI-Driven Conversations from 10K to 100K
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's engineering team shares how they evolved the Conversation Storage Service (CSS) from handling 10,000 to 100,000 concurrent AI-driven conversations. The journey involved migrating from a PostgreSQL-based transactional system to a horizontally scaled NoSQL database, introducing Kafka with conversation-level partitioning to smooth traffic spikes, and adding VegaCache to restore read-after-write consistency masked by asynchronous streaming delays. Additional optimizations include payload compression, pagination, back-pressure controls, and a metadata-driven integration layer for downstream systems like Data 360 and AI pipelines. The architecture now serves as the backbone for Salesforce's Unified Agentic Communication Platform (UACP).

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce used AI agents and deterministic optimization to cut Kubernetes idle capacity
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Hyperforce platform faced 47% idle Kubernetes capacity due to configuration sprawl across 8,000+ services. To address this, they built a Capacity Optimization Agent that uses LLMs for repository discovery and configuration parsing, but delegates all optimization decisions to a deterministic Integer Linear Programming solver. This hybrid approach overcomes the non-determinism and global reasoning limitations of pure LLM-based agents. The system generates pull requests with clear explanations and projected impacts, integrating into existing deployment pipelines to build service owner trust. The result is a closed-loop, automated workflow that reclaimed millions in infrastructure spend and is expanding to cover memory and HPA configurations.

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce improved code coverage 28% by removing boilerplate not adding tests
recent_posts.summary: A Salesforce engineer on the Security Mesh platform increased code coverage by 28% without writing any new tests by restructuring Java data models. The approach involved replacing @Data-annotated mutable classes with immutable Java records and @Value annotations, removing auto-generated boilerplate (getters, setters, utility methods) that inflated coverage denominators without representing real business logic. The Builder pattern was introduced to handle object enrichment while preserving immutability. This reduced total measured lines of code, naturally improving the coverage ratio. The post also discusses how excessive boilerplate harms AI-assisted development tools by consuming context window space and reinforcing false system contracts.

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce built autonomous lead nurturing agents that generated $100M in pipeline
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's engineering team built autonomous Lead Nurturing agents on the Agentforce platform to handle high-volume inbound leads at scale. The system generated over $100M in pipeline, created 10,000+ opportunities, and contributed to 1,500 closed deals in the SMB segment. Key engineering challenges included coordinating multiple agents under strict LLM and email rate limits, preventing duplicate outreach (early failure rates were 50-60%), and unifying fragmented CRM data. Solutions included a distributed persistent queue, a three-tier priority model, round-robin scheduling, and a unified data graph for consistent customer state. The team is now extending the system toward real-time voice-based engagement.

recent_posts.title: Keeping a Deeply Unified Platform Aligned
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Office of the Chief Architect describes how it maintains architectural coherence across a large, heterogeneous platform spanning multiple clouds, acquisitions, and product lines. Key challenges addressed include establishing a consistent tenancy model for security and data isolation, unifying metadata strategies without mandating a single implementation, and defining event-driven communication patterns that avoid tight coupling. The team balances long-term platform evolution with backward compatibility for enterprise customers who have built complex, deeply customized architectures. The re-launched Salesforce Architecture Program and Architecture Center provide opinionated guidance to help enterprise customers design scalable, reliable systems on the platform, including for emerging agentic AI use cases.

recent_posts.title: Reducing Agentforce Debugging to One Day with Query-Driven Observability
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Interactive Data Science team built a query-driven observability platform called Einstein Notebooking to debug Agentforce AI agents in production. Traditional logs and metrics couldn't expose the internal retrieval, chunking, and embedding steps that drive agent responses. By enabling direct Spark DataFrame-based queries against production indexes — including vector, keyword, and hybrid search — engineers can now inspect document chunks, embeddings, and session-level signals in a single notebook environment. A notebook-based inner loop replaced a slow multi-stage deployment workflow requiring 10+ manual steps across 3-4 repositories, cutting investigation times from two weeks to a single day. The system enforces strict security via IAM-backed access, mutual TLS, tenant-scoped contexts, and a gRPC gateway, supporting 600 users across 60+ Agentforce features and datasets exceeding 400 million records.

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce built a distributed queue to scale AI agent outreach 5x under LLM rate limits
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Agentforce team built a distributed persistent queue to orchestrate AI agent and human seller workflows under shared LLM infrastructure limits (300 RPM). The system uses a fair-share round-robin dispatcher, a three-tier priority queue (reply > intro > nudge emails), adaptive rate modulation with proactive admission control, and a dual-path architecture separating autonomous from human-review workflows. These design choices eliminated cascading rate-limit failures, prevented workload starvation, and achieved a 5x throughput increase, enabling customers to process over 10,000 leads daily.

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce built an AI sales agent generating 1M monthly CRM recommendations
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Revenue Orchestration team built a Sales Agent on Agentforce that processes hundreds of thousands of CRM opportunities nightly within a nine-hour window, generating 1.04 million monthly recommendations for 13,000 sellers. Key engineering challenges included scaling past a 300 requests-per-minute platform limit using a message queue–driven architecture, reducing per-opportunity latency from 1.35 seconds to ~600ms, and ensuring AI recommendations are explainable with citations and secured via layered access controls. The team also built a reusable, persistent platform entity for AI-generated actions shared across multiple agents, and a low-code/no-code modular architecture for enterprise configurability. In production, the system contributes to a 75% reduction in time spent on manual CRM updates.

recent_posts.title: How Salesforce Security Uses Agentforce to Triage Security Reports
recent_posts.summary: Salesforce's Cyber Security Operations Center built an AI-driven triage system using Agentforce to handle product vulnerability reports submitted by third-party researchers. The system processes unstructured inputs across formats like PDFs and spreadsheets, infers product context from a large SaaS and on-premises portfolio, and generates triage recommendations within seconds. Engineers retain final decision authority in a human-in-the-loop model. The team handled a 30% year-over-year increase in report volume without adding headcount, achieved over 90% triage accuracy, and reduced delays by replacing email submissions with a structured web form. The agent integrates directly into Slack for seamless analyst workflows and supports continuous improvement through in-workflow feedback.

recent_posts.title: Informatica’s Data Integration Platform: Running 250K Enterprise Pipelines Daily
recent_posts.summary: Shivangi Srivastava, Senior Director at Salesforce/Informatica, explains how Cloud Data Integration (CDI) evolved from a single-node engine to a distributed Spark-on-Kubernetes platform serving 5,500 enterprise customers running 250,000 daily pipelines. Key engineering decisions include extending open-source Spark into 'Spark++' for enterprise features like lineage tracking, preserving backward compatibility for existing graphical pipeline abstractions, and implementing a FinOps automation layer with three components (Cluster Lifecycle Manager, Cluster Tuner, Job Tuner) that reduces infrastructure costs by ~1.65x. The architecture separates the control plane from the data plane to maintain 99.9% availability during compute spikes.
